November 7, 2024 — Town Board

Town Board Meeting
CivicClerk page
Agenda PDF

Summary AI

The board held public hearings on a proposed 190-foot cell tower at the Wading River Fire District, the 2025 preliminary budget (7.92% tax levy increase), and several zoning code changes tied to the 2024 comprehensive plan. A series of resolutions authorizing public hearings on zoning amendments passed, most unanimously, while two amendments proposed by one board member failed on split votes.

Key actions

  • Police Officer Carly Connors was promoted to the rank of Sergeant by unanimous vote.
  • The board adopted Resolution 889 updating the industrial districts table of use regulations per the 2024 comprehensive plan; a motion to add recycling/waste uses to that table failed on a 3–2 vote.
  • The board adopted Resolution 890 updating industrial districts dimensional regulations, including a 35-foot building height standard; a motion to lower the height to 30 feet in the CI district failed on a 3–2 vote.
  • Resolutions 882–888, 891–898, and 901 authorizing public hearings on a comprehensive set of zoning map and code amendments tied to the 2024 comprehensive plan were adopted, most unanimously.
  • Resolution 903 awarding a bid for Class A biosolids improvements was adopted unanimously.
  • Resolution 909 assessing costs for remedial actions at 271 Hubbard Avenue was adopted unanimously.
  • Resolution 910 ratifying a license agreement with Ademco, Inc. to use the runway at EPCAL was adopted unanimously.
  • A CDBG grant application to Suffolk County for 2025 funding was authorized.

Public hearings & comment

  • A public hearing was held on Elite Towers/Wading River Fire District/Verizon Wireless proposal for a 190-foot concealment pole at 1503 North Country Road, Wading River; the application requires variances for use, tower setback (proposed 27 ft 10 in vs. 190 ft required), tower separation, fencing, landscaping, and rear yard; written comments are open until November 18.
  • Fire district representatives testified the tower is needed to address radio and cell communication gaps, including dropped 911 calls and inability to transmit patient data to hospitals; a Riverhead PD captain also cited police communication gaps in the area.
  • Residents testified in opposition, raising concerns about RF health standards (last updated ~30 years ago), proximity to homes and a preschool, aesthetics, property values, and inadequate community outreach; one speaker submitted a petition with 25 signatures.
  • A public hearing was held on the 2025 preliminary budget, which proposes a 7.92% town-wide tax levy increase, piercing the tax cap by 4.14% in the general fund, driven by pension, health insurance, debt service, radio replacement, and insurance cost increases; written comments are open until November 15.
  • Two board members stated they will not accept the proposed 3.2% salary increases for themselves.
  • Public hearings were also held on proposed changes to waterway/dock regulations (Chapter 293), off-street parking requirements (Chapter 301), and codifying biennial town elections; written comments on all three are open until November 18.

3:07:03For the record, Greg Bergman, Senior Planner with the Riverhead Planning Department.
3:07:06I will keep this very brief.
3:07:08This is a proposed code amendment on Chapter 293 regarding residential dock regulations.
3:07:14This came through the Conservation Advisory Council.
3:07:16We had looked at our regulations regarding residential docks.
3:07:20The CIC members felt that they were very restrictive.
3:07:23So we're making a proposed change.
3:07:26The gist of the change is that right now, the CIC members are not going to be able to do any of the regulations that we have.
3:07:28So we're going to have to make a proposed change.
3:07:28We're going to have to make a proposed change.
3:07:28The length of a residential dock is not to exceed 150 feet or 15% of the width of the waterway.
3:07:36The CIC felt that people who are buying waterfront property should have the right and enjoyment of that waterfront property.
3:07:42So we did an analysis and a look at other neighboring towns on what their residential dock regulations were.
3:07:48A lot of those other towns allowed up to one-third of the width of the waterway.
3:07:53So we sort of split the difference.
3:07:54So we are recommending a code revision, which states in Section 293,
3:07:58Section 293-60 ,
3:08:00Generally, the length of the dock shall not exceed the length needed to meet the minimum three-foot low water depth.
3:08:06However, in no case shall the length of the dock exceed 150 feet in length or exceed 25% of the width of the waterway,
3:08:14which shall be measured perpendicularly from the most seaward extension of the property taken at mean high water,
3:08:19subject to subsections two through seven below.
3:08:22Determination of the length of the dock must include the dimensions of the vessel birthed at such dock.
3:08:28So there are some just considerations also for the CAC to take into account when they're reviewing an application for a dock permit.
3:08:36But the 25% of the width of the waterway would in effect, if you had two properties across a canal from each other,
3:08:43if each dock was allowed to go 25% of the width of the waterway, including that vessel,
3:08:48that would still leave 50% of that waterway open for navigation.
3:08:52So it would not, one of the requirements is that it will not interfere with navigation,
3:08:57will not unduly interfere with public use of waterways for swimming, boating, fishing, shell fishing, etc.
3:09:03So minor change to the code. That's basically it. I'll keep it quick for time's sake.

So we are recommending a code revision, which states in Section 293, Section 293-60 , Generally, the length of the dock shall not exceed the length needed to meet the minimum three-foot low water depth. Determination of the length of the dock must include the dimensions of the vessel birthed at such dock. So there are some just considerations also for the CAC to take into account when they're reviewing an application for a dock permit. But the 25% of the width of the waterway would in effect, if you had two properties across a canal from each other, if each dock was allowed to go 25% of the width of the waterway, including that vessel, that would still leave 50% of that waterway open for navigation.
